question_text: Who was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism?
trap_type: Trap (B): Parshvanatha was the 23rd Tirthankara, immediately before Mahavira, so students pick him as the nearest earlier teacher.
pedagogical_explanation: Vardhamana Mahavira, born in the sixth century BCE near Vaishali, was the 24th and last Tirthankara of the Jains. Rishabhanatha was the first Tirthankara. Memory hook: Mahavira = 24th = Last.

question_text: Which Pallava ruler wrote the Sanskrit farce 'Mattavilasa Prahasana'?
trap_type: Trap (B): Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) was Mahendravarman's son and the better-known Pallava king, so students credit him with the work.
pedagogical_explanation: Mahendravarman I, who ruled in the early seventh century CE, composed Mattavilasa Prahasana, a satirical Sanskrit one-act play. He is also known for patronising rock-cut cave temples. Memory hook: Mahendravarman = Mattavilasa (both start with M).

question_text: Which Viceroy is regarded as the 'Father of Local Self-Government' in India because of his resolution of 1882 on local bodies?
trap_type: Trap (A): Lord Mayo's 1870 resolution on financial decentralisation was an earlier step towards local finance, so students credit him with the 1882 reform.
pedagogical_explanation: Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 encouraged elected non-official majorities in local boards and gave them real powers. Mayo's 1870 resolution only devolved certain finances to the provinces. Memory hook: Ripon = Rural and urban local bodies.

question_text: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced in British India by which Act?
trap_type: Trap (B): The 1919 Act extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans, so students think it introduced them.
pedagogical_explanation: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) provided separate electorates for Muslims for the first time. Later Acts extended the principle to other communities. Memory hook: 1909 = Minto = Muslim electorates.

question_text: Which Act redesignated the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India and ended the East India Company's role as a commercial body?
trap_type: Trap (A): The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and the China trade, so students pick it for the end of the commercial role.
pedagogical_explanation: The Charter Act of 1833 made Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India and turned the Company into a purely administrative body. The Charter Act of 1853 later added non-official members to the legislative council and opened up the civil service to competition. Memory hook: 1833 = One India, one Governor-General.

question_text: The Pamban Bridge, India's first sea bridge, connects the mainland with which island?
trap_type: Trap (A): Sriharikota is also an island on the south-eastern coast, so students pick it by region.
pedagogical_explanation: The Pamban Bridge, opened in 1914, links the mainland of Tamil Nadu with Rameswaram (Pamban) Island across the Palk Strait. Elephanta is near Mumbai and Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra. Memory hook: Pamban = Pilgrims to Rameswaram.

question_text: In Dravidian temple architecture, the monumental gateway tower at the entrance of the temple complex is called the:
trap_type: Trap (B): The Vimana is also a tall tower in Dravidian temples, but it stands over the sanctum and not over the entrance.
pedagogical_explanation: A gopuram is the large, ornate gateway tower of South Indian temples and became taller in later periods such as Chola and Vijayanagara times. The Shikhara is the tower of Nagara temples. Memory hook: Gopuram = Gate.

question_text: Phad, a long cloth scroll painting that narrates the epics of folk heroes such as Pabuji and Devnarayan, belongs to which region?
trap_type: Trap (A): Odisha's Pattachitra is also a cloth-based narrative painting, so students link the two scroll traditions.
pedagogical_explanation: Phad paintings are made by the Joshi community of Bhilwara and Shahpura in Rajasthan and are shown during storytelling performances by Bhopa priest-singers. Cheriyal scrolls come from Telangana and Patua scrolls from Bengal. Memory hook: Phad = Pabuji = Rajasthan.

question_text: India's premier first-class cricket championship, the Ranji Trophy, is named after:
trap_type: Trap (A): Duleepsinhji was Ranjitsinhji's nephew and has the Duleep Trophy named after him, so the two trophies get swapped.
pedagogical_explanation: The trophy honours Ranjitsinhji, the Jam Sahib of Nawanagar, who played Test cricket for England. The Duleep Trophy is the zonal tournament named after Duleepsinhji. Memory hook: Ranji Trophy = Ranjitsinhji.

question_text: The Keibul Lamjao National Park, known for its floating phumdis and the endangered sangai deer, lies on which lake?
trap_type: Trap (B): Dal Lake is famous for its floating gardens, so students link it with 'floating' vegetation.
pedagogical_explanation: Keibul Lamjao in Manipur is the world's only floating national park and sits on the southern part of Loktak Lake. The floating mats of vegetation, soil and organic matter are called phumdis. Memory hook: Loktak = Manipur = Sangai.

question_text: Which writ is issued to secure the release of a person who has been illegally detained?
trap_type: Trap (A): Mandamus is the best-known writ and means 'we command', so students pick it for any case where a court gives an order.
pedagogical_explanation: Habeas Corpus means 'you may have the body' and requires the detaining authority to produce the person before the court. Quo Warranto questions the legal authority of a person holding a public office. Memory hook: Habeas = Have the body.

question_text: Under which Article can Parliament create a new All-India Service common to the Union and the States if the Rajya Sabha declares by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest?
trap_type: Trap (B): Article 311 protects civil servants from dismissal without inquiry and is the best-known Article in the same Part, so students pick it.
pedagogical_explanation: Article 312 allows Parliament to legislate for new All-India Services once the Rajya Sabha passes such a resolution. Article 310 deals with the tenure of civil servants at the pleasure of the President or Governor, and Article 313 with transitional provisions. Memory hook: 312 = Create All-India Services.

question_text: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a:
trap_type: Trap (C): The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President, so students assume constitutional officers are removed in the same loose manner.
pedagogical_explanation: The proviso to Article 324(5) protects the Chief Election Commissioner's independence by giving him the same removal procedure as a Supreme Court judge, which is impeachment by Parliament. Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner. Memory hook: CEC removal = like a Supreme Court judge.

question_text: How can the Vice-President of India be removed from office before the end of the five-year term?

options.A: By impeachment by two-thirds of the total membership of each House
options.B: By a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha
options.C: By a resolution passed by two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha alone
options.D: By a resolution passed by a simple majority in a joint sitting of both Houses

trap_type: Trap (A): This is the impeachment procedure for the President under Article 61, so students apply it to the Vice-President.
pedagogical_explanation: Article 67(b) provides that the Vice-President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all its then members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, after at least fourteen days' notice. No special majority and no joint sitting is needed. Memory hook: President = Impeachment, Vice-President = Resolution.

question_text: Which winds bring most of the annual rainfall to the Tamil Nadu coast during October to December?
trap_type: Trap (A): The south-west monsoon gives most of India its rainfall, but Tamil Nadu lies in its rain shadow, so students pick it by default.
pedagogical_explanation: During the retreating monsoon, north-east winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and cause rain on the Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra coasts. Western disturbances bring winter rain to north-west India. Memory hook: Oct to Dec, Tamil Nadu = North-east monsoon.

question_text: Which lake is the deepest in the world, with a maximum depth of over 1,600 metres?
trap_type: Trap (A): Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake and the longest freshwater lake, so students pick it as the deepest.
pedagogical_explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is the deepest lake in the world and holds a very large share of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water. Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area and Victoria is Africa's largest lake by area. Memory hook: Baikal = Bottomless.

question_text: Which tidal port in Kachchh, Gujarat, was developed soon after Independence to ease the pressure on Mumbai port after the loss of Karachi port?
trap_type: Trap (C): Nhava Sheva (Jawaharlal Nehru Port) was also built to decongest Mumbai port, but much later, in the 1980s, and is in Maharashtra.
pedagogical_explanation: Kandla was the first major port developed after Partition, when Karachi went to Pakistan, and it handles large volumes of grain, salt and fertiliser. Mormugao is in Goa and Tuticorin in Tamil Nadu. Memory hook: Kandla = Kachchh = Karachi's replacement.

question_text: In Bangladesh, the main channel of the Brahmaputra is known as the:
trap_type: Trap (A): The Padma is the main channel of the Ganga in Bangladesh, which the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) joins, so students swap the two names.
pedagogical_explanation: After entering Bangladesh, the Brahmaputra flows south as the Jamuna and meets the Padma, the Ganga's channel. Their combined stream later joins the Meghna and falls into the Bay of Bengal. Dihang or Siang is its name in Arunachal Pradesh. Memory hook: Brahmaputra = Dihang in India, Jamuna in Bangladesh.

question_text: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) requirement for banks is prescribed under which provision?

options.A: Section 42 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
options.B: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
options.C: Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
options.D: Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949

trap_type: Trap (A): Section 42 of the RBI Act is the provision for the Cash Reserve Ratio, the other reserve requirement, so students swap the two.
pedagogical_explanation: Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 requires banks to maintain a percentage of their demand and time liabilities in liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities. Section 35A gives the RBI power to issue directions to banks and Section 22 deals with licensing. Memory hook: SLR = Section 24, BR Act.

question_text: Revenue deficit in the Union Budget is the excess of:

options.B: Total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings

trap_type: Trap (B): This is the definition of fiscal deficit, the best-known budget deficit, so students use it for revenue deficit.
pedagogical_explanation: Revenue deficit means the government's day-to-day spending exceeds its revenue (tax and non-tax) receipts, which implies borrowing even for consumption. Fiscal deficit minus interest payments is the primary deficit. Memory hook: Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure minus Revenue receipts.

question_text: Which money market instrument is an unsecured short-term promissory note issued mainly by highly rated corporates to raise funds?
trap_type: Trap (A): A Certificate of Deposit is also an unsecured short-term money market instrument, but it is issued by banks and not by corporates.
pedagogical_explanation: Commercial Paper lets companies with a good credit rating borrow directly from investors for short periods. Treasury Bills are issued by the Government and call money is inter-bank borrowing for one day. Memory hook: CP = Corporate Paper, CD = Customer Deposit at a bank.

question_text: A person who can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects clearly (myopia) is corrected using which lens?
trap_type: Trap (A): A convex lens corrects hypermetropia (far-sightedness), the opposite defect, so students swap the two.
pedagogical_explanation: In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. A concave lens of suitable power diverges the rays so the image forms on the retina. Memory hook: Myopia = Minus power = Concave.

question_text: The painful burning sensation caused by a red ant's sting is mainly due to which acid?
trap_type: Trap (A): Acetic acid is the familiar kitchen acid of vinegar, so students pick it as the most common weak acid.
pedagogical_explanation: Red ants inject formic acid (methanoic acid), and rubbing a mild base such as baking soda on the sting neutralises it and gives relief. The name formic comes from the Latin word for ant. Memory hook: Formic = Formica = Ant.

question_text: In the chloroplast, the light-independent (dark) reactions of photosynthesis take place in the:
trap_type: Trap (B): The grana are the stacks of thylakoids where the light reactions occur, so students place all of photosynthesis there.
pedagogical_explanation: The light reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the grana, producing ATP and NADPH. These are used in the stroma, the fluid matrix, where the Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugars. Memory hook: Grana = Light, Stroma = Sugar.

question_text: The ABO blood group system was discovered by:
trap_type: Trap (A): William Harvey is the famous scientist who described the circulation of blood, so students link every blood-related discovery to him.
pedagogical_explanation: Karl Landsteiner identified the A, B and O blood groups, which made safe blood transfusion possible, and received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1930. Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine and Pasteur worked on germ theory and vaccines. Memory hook: Landsteiner = Labelled the blood groups.
